<reason>A won the comparison between the actual regulatory alternatives. Its concrete pre-release design tests undermined B’s repeated claim that conduct-based regulation necessarily waits for injury. A also identified a meaningful cost of blanket overnight and session restrictions: obstructing support that encourages healthy disengagement. B established a plausible residual risk of attachment without manipulation, but did not adequately weigh that risk against A’s safeguards and the access costs of its additional restrictions. A’s later speeches sharpened this unresolved burden more effectively.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s distinction between demonstrated design risk and demonstrated injury directly answered B’s pressure questions. Combined with its distinction between availability and inducement, this exposed the weakness in B’s prevention-versus-waiting framing.</best_rebuttal>
